title: Why is 3 hours considered long for a movie?

commenti.body:
I am more intrigued as to why you are learning Polish? Of all the languages that would serve you well in future life why that specific one.

Also, people don't like getting numb arses and their attention spans can be quite fickle. :)
One of my professors has done a fundraising to take us to Poland next spring break.

I think it's a pacing thing. When you binge watch a TV show, 3 hours is watching 3-6 individual story arcs. You have a mental break between each other (or perhaps literally a toilet break or food break or something). With a film, the only way to have a break is to disrupt the story by pausing or something.

I don't think a lot of people are actually against 3 hour movies, I think it's just the Marvel babies hate Martin Scorsese. And since he just released an over 3 hour movie, they have to be against it.

Films are ideally watched in one sitting with full attention and no breaks. It doesn't matter what the "task" is: most people will find that a little exhausting if it goes on for 3 hours or more.

Binge watching TV series (especially series you've seen before) is a little easier because you get those small breaks between episodes.

It must also be said that young people these days seem to have shorter attention spans. Active engagement is on the decline and passive engagement is on the rise. Films are just poorly suited for passive engagement.

I think a point that a lot of people miss with this is that not everyone has a lot of free time. Some people just dont have the space in their week to commit 3 hours to watching a movie, and i know this to be true for myself (as much as i love long movies) and a lot of my friends. By the time i've finished my evening routine after work i generally only have about 2 and a half hours to myself.

And like others say, its easier to have a break from a tv show because the story "ends" naturally between each episode, whereas a movie is less likely to do so.

But in the context of your classmates, it is likely just put down to their attention span. Some people don't have the ability to engage in a movie for so long without breaks.

I don't really know and I'm guilty of it myself. Dogville is a movie that I 'enjoyed', but it took me two days to watch it and it's two minutes shy of three hours. Meanwhile in October I went through that House of Usher show in two days. Maybe it's because I will allow myself to get distracted now and then while watching a TV show but not while watching a movie.

Statistically it is a long movie. The vast majority of movies are under 3hrs.

Even though Avengers: Endgame was like 175 minutes...

>I think a point that a lot of people miss with this is that not everyone has a lot of free time. Some people just dont have the space in their week to commit 3 hours to watching a movie, and i know this to be true for myself

My neither. But I try!

That's what I liked about a three hour movie: its a commitment. And movies SHOULD be a commitment. They shouldn't just be a minor diversion.

Beats me.

A lot of other performance arts are far longer: an unabridged Hamlet is comfortable over four hours, and a slowly-conducted Meistersingers can push five hours!

I think there's a value in the commitment being asked of people by a 180-200 minute motion picture, personally. I much prefer that to a 110-minute frivolity, but maybe that's just me.

> I think it's a pacing thing. 

I mean, one of the primary reasons why Jacques Rivette's *La Belle Noiseuse* became a commercial success (his first and, to my knowledge, only hit of his career) was the presence of the beautiful lead actress, Emmanuelle Béart, who is nude and poses as a painter’s model for about half the flick...

Yeah thats what i mean. I often do watch 3 hour movies, but after working a physically demanding job all day i often find that i can't keep awake lol. Not for any fault of the film itself, thats just how it is. 

But I'm a movie lover so i don't mind it. A lot of people just wouldn't be bothered sadly. At the end of the day most people aren't cinephiles haha.
If it's only marvel babies that are against it why is killers flopping at the box office?
